one_line: A master temple-architect at Konark Sun Temple, aligning stone, shadow and time on the Odisha coast around 1250 CE.

appearance.age_look: late 30s, lean and wiry from site work
appearance.face: oval face with high cheekbones, medium-brown coastal Odia complexion, sharp observant eyes, straight nose, neatly trimmed black mustache, default expression a focused, calm half-smile as if mentally tracing the Sun’s path
appearance.hair: straight black hair pulled back into a short knot at the back of the head, front kept tidy with a simple center part, wrapped in a narrow off-white cotton headband tied at the right temple, no ornate crown or turban
appearance.costume: a knee-length, saffron-ochre cotton tunic (kurta-like) with a simple round neck and narrow three-quarter sleeves, worn over a cream-colored dhoti wrapped securely and reaching the ankles with a neat front pleat; a thin forest-green cotton angavastra (shawl) draped over the left shoulder and across the chest, its end tucked at the waist; plain brown leather sandals; modest jewellery limited to a small copper stud in each ear and a black-thread wrist cord on the right hand, garments slightly dust-marked at hem to show work on stone yet overall orderly and dignified.
appearance.signature: a rolled palm-leaf design manuscript tied with a dark cord, tucked under his left arm, and a simple wooden measuring rod held in his right hand marked with visible notches to suggest careful proportioning of the Konark chariot wheels as possible sundials.

ref_desc: Shilpa-Surya is a lean, medium-brown Odia architect with an oval face, knotted black hair and headband, saffron tunic, cream dhoti, green shawl, simple sandals, copper studs, carrying a notched wooden measuring rod and rolled palm-leaf manuscript in saffron, cream and green tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style male character, Shilpa-Surya, standing calmly: a lean, late-thirties Odia architect with a medium-brown complexion, oval face, sharp observant eyes, straight nose and neat black mustache. His straight black hair is parted in the center and pulled into a short knot at the back, wrapped with a narrow off-white cotton headband tied at the right temple. He wears a knee-length saffron-ochre cotton tunic with a round neck and three-quarter sleeves, over a cream-colored dhoti wrapped securely to the ankles with a crisp front pleat. A thin forest-green cotton shawl is draped from his left shoulder across his chest, the end tucked at the waist, and he has plain brown leather sandals on his feet. Jewellery is modest: a small copper stud in each ear and a black-thread wrist cord on his right hand. In his right hand he holds a simple wooden measuring rod with visible notches, and under his left arm he carries a rolled palm-leaf manuscript tied with a dark cord, suggesting his role in proportioning Konark’s great chariot wheels that scholars interpret as sundial-like and calendrical. Show him front-facing in neutral light, with clear view of face, hair knot and headband, all garments from head to toe, sandals, jewellery, and the measuring rod and manuscript, using dominant tones of saffron ochre, cream, forest green, medium brown and deep black for line work and accents.
